title: G. Stop Spot
statement:
You are given an array a of size n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ m).

Consider all m! permutations of the array [1, 2, …, m]. For any permutation p, define the array b_p as the array formed by concatenating the array a and the permutation p. More formally, b_p = [a_1, a_2, …, a_n, p_1, p_2, …, p_m].

Let f(i) denote the number of permutations p such that the array b_p contains exactly i palindromic^{∗} subarrays of even length.

Your task is to compute ∑_{i=0}^{10^100} f(i)^{i+1}.

Since the answer may be large, it should be computed modulo 998,244,353.

^{∗}An array [c_1, c_2, …, c_k] is said to be palindromic if c_i = c_{k+1-i} for all 1 ≤ i ≤ k.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each testcase contains two integers n and m (1 ≤ m ≤ n ≤ 10^6).

The second line of each testcase contains n integers a_1, a_2, …, a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ m) — the elements of the array.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n over all test cases does not exceed 10^6.

For each testcase, print a single integer on a new line — ∑_{i=0}^{10^100} f(i)^{i+1} modulo 998,244,353.

In the first test case, n=4, m=3, and a=[3,1,2,1].

Let's list all permutations and calculate the number of palindromic subarrays of even length:

Thus, we have f(0) = 4, f(1) = 1, f(2) = 1, and f(i) = 0 for all i > 2. Hence, the answer is 4^1 + 1^2 + 1^3 = 6.

Input:
```
54 33 1 2 11 119 44 1 2 1 3 3 1 2 16 31 1 3 1 1 110 64 4 1 2 1 3 3 1 2 1
```

Output:
```
61124896025814006753
```
